newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.02 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.02 percent to close at 1.0153 to the dollar in the commercial foregin exchange market, with players speculating on a possible new drop in the real-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The current mini-band, between 1.015 and 1.020 per dollar, was set Friday by the Central Bank.
The real was traded for most of the session between 1.0154 and 1.0156 reais per dollar because some banks bought dollars expecting a drop in the mini-band today.
Since the Central Bank did not intervene in the market, the real gained some ground in the end of the day.
Dollar inflows also helped the local currency's rebound, traders said. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Tuesday surplus of $100 million.
Dealers said they still expect a drop in the mini-band in coming days.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0203 to the dollar, down 0.03 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended flat at 1.034 per greenback.
